summary: The head-binding waiver's core factual claim is independently verified and is STRONGER than the waiver states: the branch changes zero product code relative to origin/main, and every src/ change in the unproven delta is strictly upstream and already merged to main. The discarded-run disclosure fix is genuine, not papering-over. All four verification records are reliable (runner_direct, timed_out=false, unchanged worktree/head hashes). All 3 review-surface violations are honestly acknowledged with explicit verdict-deliberately-NOT-recorded evidence, and no stale-head verdict was passed off as current. However, two of the structured observations added this round specifically to close gate:common_judgment_spine and gate:responsibility_authority contain claims that do not hold: the integration lane claims a VET-S-6 boundary scenario it does not execute, and the unit lane names a target file that does not exist. A gate closed on an observation asserting coverage the lane does not run is the exact vacuous-evidence pattern this Story exists to eliminate.

findings.detail: The integration observation scenario reads 'boundary_condition: VET-S-6 asserts the .spec.ts gate still counts more than zero specs after the 17 deletions'. The integration lane command is node --test over 8 named files, none of which exercises the .spec.ts gate; grep for run-e2e-ts-specs across those 8 files returns EMPTY. The real VET-S-6 coverage is in the acceptance spec, which runs in the E2E lane. Fix: remove that scenario line from the integration observation.

The unit observation lists target test/managed-worktree-gate.test.js, which does not exist (ls reports No such file or directory). The AC-4/VET-S-4 bypassed-branch coverage it describes is real but lives in test/e2e/story-vibepro-managed-worktree-gate-main.test.js. The substance is truthful; the cited path is not. The sibling target test/execution-state.test.js does exist and does assert the agent_review derivation, so only the one path is wrong.

Both observations paraphrase AC-6 as the .spec.ts gate counting more than zero specs. The actual test asserts the gate still fails closed on an empty spec set, a different and stronger property. Minor wording drift, but drift in exactly the asserting-about versus executing direction the Story targets.

The waiver asserts integration bound to 06450d62 equals CURRENT HEAD. Current HEAD is b9ed51a3, recorded after the waiver. git diff 06450d62..b9ed51a3 is .vibepro/config.json only so the substance is unaffected, but by the waiver's own standard the statement should be restated rather than left as-is.

inspection.summary: Independently re-derived every head-binding claim from git rather than accepting the waiver text: merge-base ea5e90fc, git diff --name-only ea5e90fc..HEAD -- src/ bin/ EMPTY, git merge-base --is-ancestor 31d84833 origin/main TRUE, git log 3be3ed55..HEAD exactly four commits, git diff 06450d62..b9ed51a3 config only. Verified the discarded-run disclosure documents and their cross-reference. Read all four verification-run JSONs and the verification-evidence.json observations, then checked each observation claim against the actual test files and run logs, which is where the two medium findings came from. Ran node scripts/lint-e2e-product-execution.mjs exit 0 over 66 files and review violations --json showing 3 of 3 acknowledged.

judgment_delta: Initial concern: a waiver accepting four records bound to two non-HEAD commits, written by the implementing agent, is the classic shape of evidence laundering and I expected to block -> Final needs_changes: the head-binding argument is not only sound but understates itself, and the unit-discard disclosure is genuinely sufficient rather than papering-over. What moved me off pass was that the observations were added specifically to close two gates, so I checked them rather than reading them, and two claims fail. Two string edits, hence needs_changes rather than block.
